crashRecovery.method: A 28 MiB checkpoint save (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, upsert checkpoint, delete updates, commit) is started and the owner worker is terminated after a random delay in [0, 1.1 x save round trip]; a new worker takes the copy's Web Lock, installs the pool and opens with the quick check. 50 kills per row.

rows.result: corrupt after 1 kill: hot journal present, quick_check 'Tree 9 page 9 cell 0: invalid page number 7428'
corrupt after 2 to 6 kills, same quick_check failure
50/50 committed: terminate() lets the running synchronous WASM call finish, so no kill lands mid-commit
50/50 (43 rolled back through the hot journal, 7 committed); again 50/50 (34 rolled back, 16 committed) in the full run
50/50 (48 rolled back, 2 committed) once installs retry in a fresh worker
50/50 committed; closing the tab mid-commit: 10/10 left a hot journal and all 10 recovered
50/50 (29 rolled back, 21 committed); tab closes 10/10 (10 hot journals)

crashRecovery.cause: sqlite-wasm-vfs 0.2.0 sahpool's xCheckReservedLock always reports a reserved lock, so SQLite's hasHotJournal never treats a left-over journal as hot and never rolls back an interrupted commit. Native SQLite given the same database and journal rolled back to a file passing quick_check and integrity_check. sqlite.org's JavaScript opfs-sahpool reports real lock state (forum:b2fbb61642); sqlite-wasm-vfs 0.3.0 tracks lock levels.
crashRecovery.lockRelease: A dead worker's Web Lock can be granted before its sync access handles close (WebKit, Firefox): the next install fails with NoModificationAllowedError and succeeds when retried in a fresh worker after 50 ms.

nativeFindings: A WAL-mode file (header bytes 18-19 = 2,2) is accepted by native `slop inspect`, `get` and `apply`; the writer rewrites it to rollback mode and leaves a -shm file. The comment on file::connect says such a file is refused. The browser cannot open it (sahpool has no shared memory) and refuses it as a storage failure.
`slop inspect` on a WAL-mode file leaves -wal and -shm files beside it.
A file truncated mid-page (1,000 bytes short) opens and edits natively, and in the browser.
